meta.title: Antigravity Executor
meta.description: Delegate coding tasks to the signed-in Antigravity desktop agent and watch every turn live in a War Room dashboard. The dashboard has two entry points: the dsh sidebar panel icon, and the standalone page on http://127.0.0.1:18420 — both are the exact same page (same-origin embedded, not two separate implementations), and follow the host light/dark theme. It provides a five-stage lifecycle stepper, a streaming tool-call timeline (with category filter pills, automatic folding of runs of read-only exploration, per-step accordion detail and four verdict badges), dual-window account quota gauges (5h + weekly) with reset countdowns, reserve markers and a per-turn burn delta, one-click emergency abort and cooldown skip, hot runtime policy switches that can be persisted to the config file, session management with memory-preserving rollover, brain artifact browsing, and a four-tab Universal Inspector split pane: red/green git diffs, terminal and test output with exit-code badges and error tails, a task-plan checklist progress bar, and a live HTML/3D preview with WebGL context recycling and an inline runtime-error capture bar — all refreshed when a turn settles. The console is served by a zero-dependency node:http + SSE server that frees its port on reload. It also retains the adaptive three-way task mode (surgical engineering, creative visual density with a Pass-1 gate, document office/report automation, with session-sticky inheritance), retry and complexity auto-escalation from flash to pro (still bounded by the quota guard), RPC settlement returning within seconds, an in-process serial queue, untruncated long reports, dual-window 5h/weekly quota guards, split destructive-vs-escape circuit breakers, human-like inter-turn pacing, dead-session self-heal, a 60s hanging-command circuit breaker, zero-side-effect pre-turn git snapshots with precise one-click rollback, structured command exit-code extraction with fake-success interception, memory-preserving long-session rollover, and git snapshots inlined into every result.
